steps.title: Power off and remove the SIM tray
steps.instruction: Hold the power button and confirm power off. Eject the SIM tray with the SIM tool.
steps.visualCheck: Screen is black and the SIM tray lies on the mat next to the phone.

steps.title: Open the back cover
steps.instruction: Warm the back cover edges, then slide a plastic pick around the seam. Lift the cover from the bottom only a few centimetres: the fingerprint flex is still attached at the top.
steps.visualCheck: The back cover is lifted like a book hinge and the fingerprint flex cable is visible, still intact.

commonMistakes.description: Pulling the cover fully away before disconnecting the fingerprint flex tears the cable.
commonMistakes.looksLike: Back cover held far from the phone body with a thin ribbon cable stretched between them.

steps.title: Remove the motherboard shield screws
steps.instruction: Remove the Phillips screws holding the motherboard shield. Lay them out on the mat in the same pattern as they came out: they are not all the same length.
steps.visualCheck: Screws are laid out in a pattern on the mat and the shield lifts off the top of the board.

commonMistakes.description: Dropping all screws in one pile makes it easy to put a long screw in a short hole later.
commonMistakes.looksLike: Several screws together in a single pile or loose in a cup.

steps.title: Disconnect the battery
steps.instruction: With a plastic spudger, pry the battery connector straight up off the board. Do this before touching any other connector.
steps.visualCheck: The battery connector is lifted off its socket and bent slightly away so it can't touch the board.

commonMistakes.description: Unplugging the display or another flex while the battery is connected can short the board.
commonMistakes.looksLike: A tool or fingers at a connector other than the battery's while the battery connector is still seated.

commonMistakes.description: Metal tweezers or a screwdriver on the battery connector can bridge the contacts.
commonMistakes.looksLike: A shiny metal tool tip touching the battery connector.

steps.title: Disconnect the display and charging flex
steps.instruction: Now that the battery is disconnected, pry up the display connector and the charging-board flex.
steps.visualCheck: Display and charging flex connectors are lifted off the board.

steps.title: Swap the battery
steps.instruction: Pull the adhesive tabs slowly at a low angle to release the battery. Never pry under the battery with metal, never bend or puncture it.
steps.visualCheck: The old battery is out, flat and undamaged, and the new battery is seated in the frame.

commonMistakes.description: Levering a lithium battery with a metal tool can puncture it and start a fire.
commonMistakes.looksLike: A tool pushed under the battery, or the battery visibly bent.

steps.title: Refit the shield screws
steps.instruction: Put each screw back in the hole it came from. The long screw goes only in the marked corner.
steps.visualCheck: The shield is back on and every screw is seated flush.

commonMistakes.description: A long screw in a short hole can crack the board underneath.
commonMistakes.looksLike: The longest screw being driven into a hole other than the marked corner, or a screw head sitting high.

steps.title: Reconnect flexes, then the battery last
steps.instruction: Press the display and charging flex connectors home first. Reconnect the battery last, then close the cover.
steps.visualCheck: All connectors seated; the battery connector is the last one pressed down.

commonMistakes.description: Reconnecting the battery before the display can damage the display driver.
commonMistakes.looksLike: Battery connector pressed down while the display flex is still loose.

session.summary: The repair went through 8 steps. Second Hands stopped 1 likely mistake before damage was done and asked 1 clarifying question. 0 warnings were overridden by the technician. Next time, disconnect the battery before reaching for any other connector, and keep screws laid out in order.
